data.answer:
**The latest estimate is $63.7 billion, or 2.5 per cent of GDP, for cultural and creative activity in 2022–23**, reported in the 2026 Australian IP Report.[1] However, this is not a valuation of copyright alone: generating IP, such as copyright, is just one of four criteria used to define the activities included.[2]

A more copyright-specific study estimated that **industries relying on copyright protection contributed $124.1 billion in 2018**, equivalent to 6.8 per cent of GDP. Those industries also accounted for 8.3 per cent of Australian employment and generated $4.8 billion in exports.[3]

**These figures should not be treated as a time series.** The 2024 report put cultural and creative activity at $122.3 billion, or 6.2 per cent of GDP, in 2019–20. The methodology was updated in 2024, and the 2025 report explicitly says the new figures are not comparable with previous Australian IP reports.[4]

Another indicator of copyright’s economic value is licensing income: **over $800 million was paid through collecting societies in 2023–24** to artists, musicians, writers and screen industry workers.[5]
